description: Who We Are You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today. We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover. Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI. Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate. Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale. About the team Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, ecommerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people. About the role We’re looking for an experienced applied scientist to help set LCM’s research direction and work directly on its most demanding scientific problems. This is a hands-on individual contributor role in a flat team of around 30 engineers, with no direct reports. You will mentor colleagues and contribute to hiring, but you will not manage people. We define how a capability will be evaluated before developing it, and use that evidence to guide training and deployment decisions. You will help decide which research questions deserve investment, design and run experiments, and develop training methods that can be used across applications. The role requires deep expertise in a core area of model training and the judgment to connect that work with decisions about data, evaluation and deployment. Scientists and engineers work together from the first experiment through to production evaluation, and you will take scientific responsibility for agreed research projects. A central research goal is to learn from a continuous stream of billions of user sessions across the portfolio and turn useful signals into regular updates to model weights. What the role involves Develop the research agenda with the team, identifying questions that affect model quality, training efficiency or downstream results. Use experiments to decide which approaches warrant larger training runs and which should be revised or stopped. Lead selected research projects through implementation, training and evaluation, staying directly involved in writing code, inspecting data, debugging runs and analysing failures. Establish evaluation methods that separate real improvements from leakage, noise and benchmark overfitting, and work with portfolio teams to test whether offline gains hold in controlled online experiments. Mentor scientists and engineers through joint research, experiment reviews and technical discussion, and advise on work that crosses project boundaries. Contribute to hiring, publish research and support the release of models, benchmarks and training methods where the work and data can be shared. Research areas The initial focus will depend on your expertise and the team’s priorities. We expect substantial depth in one of the two areas below, with the ability to contribute to decisions across the other. Pre-training and representations We continue pre-training open-weight models on commerce data. Research questions include how to represent users and catalogues, how to combine data from different businesses, and how to allocate compute effectively. Work may include: Studying data mixtures, scaling behaviour and training schedules to guide the next run. Designing sequences from user histories, merchant catalogues and market data, including alignment between text and semantic IDs for users, items and merchants. Developing mid-training methods for capability acquisition, context extension and retention of general capabilities. Evaluating synthetic data and distillation methods through controlled experiments, including the trade-offs between quality, inference cost and latency. Studying transfer across languages, markets and commerce categories, with evaluations for new users and items and for performance on future data. Tabular foundation models are a possible specialisation, including pre-training and in-context learning on structured commerce data. Post-training and continual learning We train LCM for commerce tasks and a range of agent applications, including customer-facing assistants and agents that carry out business operations. We also develop continual learning methods that turn new interactions into regular updates to model weights. Work may include: Developing supervised fine-tuning, preference optimisation and reinforcement learning methods, using verifiable outcomes or learned reward models. Turning session histories, searches, clicks, purchases, repeat orders and operator feedback into training examples and rewards, accounting for exposure bias, delayed feedback and the difference between observed engagement and incremental business value. Studying data selection, replay and update frequency so models learn from new interactions without losing established capabilities. Training and evaluating decision models that choose rankings, offers and promotions, using offline learning and off-policy evaluation to estimate policy value and uncertainty and inform controlled online experiments. Training models for multi-turn conversations and multi-step agent workflows, including understanding user intent, planning, tool use, maintaining context, recovering from errors and verifying outcomes. This includes building RL environments with simulated users and catalogues, and testing whether gains transfer to real interactions within defined permissions and business rules. Calibrating reward models and LLM-based graders against expert judgments and observed outcomes, and investigating reward hacking and other unintended effects. Developing automated experimentation methods that propose and test changes to training recipes, prompts, tools or agent control flow, with held-out evaluations and regression checks. How we evaluate the work Research should produce evidence that supports a training or deployment decision. We use strong baselines, including existing production systems, and weigh model quality against compute requirements, inference cost and latency. Experiments should be reproducible, with ablations, uncertainty estimates and failure analysis. They must account for temporal leakage, changes in the data distribution and differences between companies and markets. Negative results are valuable when they explain a limitation or stop further investment in an approach that does not work. The work also involves data provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy-aware handling of customer histories, together with our data and engineering teams. In the first three months, we expect you to establish a focused research programme, resolve an important training or evaluation question, and work with the relevant teams to test the resulting method in a downstream application. Minimum qualifications A PhD or equivalent industry research experience in machine learning, computer science, statistics or a related field. At least eight years of research or applied science experience in machine learning, including doctoral research, with at least four years leading research directions that were published or reached production. Substantial experience developing and training models, with deep expertise in pre-training, post-training or reinforcement learning relevant to the areas above. A record of original contributions, shown through research papers, released models, benchmarks, open-source projects or significant advances in deployed systems. Scientific leadership: choosing research directions, resolving difficult technical questions and helping experienced colleagues make better decisions. Sound experimental and statistical judgment, including examples where the evidence changed your approach and the ability to recognise when the evidence does not support a conclusion. Strong Python and PyTorch skills and the ability to work independently in a shared research codebase. Research on large language models requires hands-on experience with distributed training. Clear communication and a collaborative approach to disagreement, review and mentoring. Preferred qualifications Experience with recommender systems, generative retrieval, semantic IDs, continual learning, synthetic data, distillation or tabular foundation models. Familiarity with commerce data and online experimentation. We do not expect expertise in every area. What we offer Influence over LCM’s research agenda and which questions the team invests in. Proprietary commerce data, B300 and H200 GPUs for large-scale training, and external models for evaluation and benchmarking. The opportunity to take research from early experiments through publication and deployment, working directly with portfolio teams on products used by millions of people. Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems. An uncapped budget to recruit and mentor research interns for your projects, with access to candidates through our connections with leading universities. Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants. A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. Dernier échange et proposition : alignement final et discussion autour du package. Nous nous engageons à te faire un retour sous 7 jours maximum à chaque étape. 🚀 Prêt(e) à donner une nouvelle dimension à ta carrière Product ? Si tu veux travailler sur des produits IA concrets, relever des défis complexes et évoluer aux côtés d'une communauté d'experts, on serait ravis d'échanger avec toi ! 👉 Postule et construisons ensemble les produits intelligents de demain. Work on projects scoped in weeks rather than quarters, prioritising rapid iteration and customer impact. Work closely with the ML team. description: Lemonway est un établissement de paiement agréé, au cœur de la nouvelle économie européenne. Analyser les données produit et en tirer des lectures actionnables : évolution des indicateurs, écarts par rapport aux objectifs, adoption des fonctionnalités, retours utilisateurs ; proposer des recommandations aux PM et au leadership. Mettre en place des automatisations IA pour récupérer et consolider les insights go-to-market internes (retours Sales, Support, Customer Success, tickets) et les rendre exploitables par l’équipe Produit. 🗂️ Pilotage produit et rituels Aider à centraliser et qualifier les insights et product requests avant leur analyse et leur priorisation. Contribuer aux analyses de marché et benchmarks concurrentiels pour alimenter la roadmap et le positionnement. Aider au suivi de l’adoption des fonctionnalités après mise en production et remonter les retours aux PM. Excellentes compétences rédactionnelles en français et en anglais (équivalent B2/C1 minimum). Bonnes compétences en communication et en organisation. description: About Us Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected. About the Role As Project Quality Manager, you own the Project & Program pillar of Harmattan’s Quality organization. You set the quality standards that carry every programme from first prototypes through to mass production. You lead the Project Quality Engineers and act as the quality counterpart of Program Management, Engineering and our institutional customers. Your work keeps quality gates rigorous at the right level for each development phase, in line with ISO 9001 / EN 9100. Responsibilities Leadership & Team Building Lead, coach and grow the Project Quality Engineering team, and allocate engineers across active programmes. Act as the quality counterpart of Program Management, Engineering leads and institutional customers. Standardize project quality practices across programmes and turn lessons learned into company standards. Quality Gates & Product Development Own quality gate governance from EVT to PVT and transfer to mass production, including go/no-go recommendations. Drive advanced product quality planning (APQP / EN 9145): quality plans, DFMEA / PFMEA, special characteristics and control plans. Ensure design and development quality per EN 9100: design reviews, verification and validation evidence, configuration and change control. Arbitrate open development non-conformities, risks and deviations, and lead structured problem solving. Customer Deliverables & Performance Deliver customer quality documentation, including quality and management plans and qualification and acceptance files. Prepare customer audits and delivery verification readiness together with Site Quality. Align with Supplier Quality and Industrialization on first article inspection and production readiness. Define and report project quality KPIs, including risks, non-conformities and gate readiness, reviewed regularly with Programs. Candidate Requirements Engineering degree (MSc or equivalent) in quality, aeronautical, mechanical, electronics or systems engineering. 8+ years in project, programme or design quality in aerospace, defense, automotive or high-tech hardware. 2 to 3+ years leading a team, or leading quality on a full programme. Strong command of EN 9100 / ISO 9001, APQP / PPAP (EN 9145), DFMEA / PFMEA, control plans, design reviews and 8D. Experience taking complex electromechanical or embedded products through EVT / DVT / PVT to serial production. Structured and pragmatic, applying the right level of rigor per phase and holding firm at gates when needed. Knowledge of AQAP 2110 and defense customer requirements is a plus; comfort with Jira and Confluence. Regular on-site presence at the production site, alongside Paris-based work. Fluency in French and English required. We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI. Find Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

Database and Query Languages: Experience with SQL, including constructing and optimizing complex queries for large datasets; experience with BigQuery or other cloud-based querying platforms is a strong advantage. Computational Finance: Exposure to computational finance concepts, with familiarity in using quantitative methods and tools for finance-related applications. Statistics and Data Analysis: Strong statistical knowledge, including probability distributions, hypothesis testing, and data sampling methods. Ability to apply statistical analysis techniques to analyze financial data. Mathematics and Machine Learning: Solid foundation in mathematical principles, including linear algebra and calculus, with a focus on regression analysis. Exposure to machine learning and deep learning algorithms and methods in the presence of sparse data, including common imputation approaches. . description: Functie Reliability engineer Beschrijving functie De reliability engineer is een productie specialist die de totale levensduur van installatie bestudeert en analyseert hoe het bedrijf omgaat met investeringen en onderhoud van assets. De reliability engineer is de expert in het identificeren van potentiële risico’s en het voorkomen van stilstanden. Daar problemen moeilijk volledig te voorkomen zijn, geeft de reliability engineer adviezen hoe te handelen bij storingen die plaatsvinden. Het doel is te voorkomen dat fouten in productiesystemen optreden. De reliability engineer analyseert tevens de veiligheidsrisico’s geassocieerd met installatie fouten. Ter voorkoming van stilstand maakt de reliability engineer onderhoudsschema’s en analyseert statistische gegevens die helpen te voorspellen wanneer en hoe fouten voor kunnen komen. De reliability engineer ontwikkelt inspectie criteria die gebruikt worden om de asset health te monitoren. Om dit te kunnen bereiken maakt de reliability engineer gebruik van een aantal technieken. Voorlopige gevaren analyse: Preliminary hazard analysis is de initiële identificatie van potentiële gevaren en fouten in een productie proces of systeem Failure modes and effect analysis ( FMEA): Betreft het opsommen van de manieren dat een proces of systeem kan falen en wat de consequenties hiervan zijn. Criticality analysis: bepaalt hoe ernstig de consequenties zijn van een asset fout voor het productiesysteem van het bedrijf. Onderhoudbaarheid: gedetailleerde informatie hoe efficiënt en betrouwbaar het bedrijf een onderdeel kan repareren. Foutenboom analyse: onderzoek van een systeem fout door naar de kleinere voorafgaande gebeurtenissen te kijken die hebben bijgedragen aan de systeem fout Taken Trouble shooting Faciliteren van root cause analyse in geval van complexe, multidisciplinaire afwijkingen/storingen waar de uitvoerende teams niet uitkomen Daily problem solving Continue verbeteren Periodieke analyse op performance killers en cost drivers om van daaruit middels verbetervoorstellen bij te dragen aan een maximale beschikbaarheid & betrouwbaarheid van installaties tegen minimale kosten Innovatief denken m.b.t. het verlagen van de kosten en verhogen van de betrouwbaarheid Leiden/faciliteren van verbeterteams c.q. verbeterprojecten Change Management Beoordelen van wijzigingen op technische haalbaarheid met het bestaande machinepark. Vanuit procurement komen verzoeken op het gebied van grondstof wijzigingen ( andere leverancier, andere specificaties ed.) Begeleiden van proeven vanuit de technische kant op de machines Installatie nieuwe machines / introductie nieuwe producten Technische beschikbaarheid & betrouwbaarheid Evalueren van preventief onderhoud en voorstellen doen ter verbetering met als doel het verhogen van de beschikbaarheid van het machinepark Het verlagen van onderhoudskosten door het optimaliseren van onderhoudsconcepten en doorvoeren van technische verbeteringen. Investeringsprojecten Participeren in investeringsprojecten om de onderhoudbaarheid te borgen en het inregelen van onderhoud en spare parts. Inbrengen van technische kennis en ervaringen. Toezien op naleving van de standaard op gebied van onderdelen en installaties. Onderhoudsstrategie bepalen Opstellen van effectieve onderhoudsconcepten zodat onderhoud van de installaties op de meest efficiënte en effectieve manier kan worden gerealiseerd tegen zo laag mogelijke kosten Borgen van compliance; het inregelen van wettelijke inspecties en keuringen en toezien op tijdige uitvoering daarvan. description: About Black Forest Labs We’re the team building the foundational layer for visual intelligence: multimodal models trained jointly on images, video, audio, and action to see, generate, and understand the world. Our founding team pioneered latent diffusion and Stable Diffusion, the breakthroughs that made generative AI accessible to millions. With FLUX, we're pushing into generative media at scale, machines that act in the physical world, and emerging applications in computer use. Our FLUX models top public benchmarks and run in production in some of the world's biggest platforms. We're a small, fast growing research lab competing with the largest companies in the world. From our labs in Freiburg to San Francisco, we're building what comes next. Why This Role We develop AI models and run the infrastructure on which those models are trained, deployed, and served to customers. Securing that infrastructure comes with real challenges: researchers need flexible access to significant compute resources, production systems need strong isolation and reliability, and model assets and customer data need protection throughout their lifecycle. Our research and production infrastructure teams design, build, and operate these systems. We're looking for an experienced, hands-on security engineer to partner with them as we grow: someone who can dig into the details, do the engineering, and work alongside those teams to improve our defensive posture. This is an engineering role: you'll spend time reading code, understanding systems, debugging problems, and shipping changes. What You’ll Work On These are the areas this role draws from; you're not expected to cover them all at once: Infrastructure architecture and isolation. Understand how our research and production environments fit together, identify consequential attack paths, and work with infrastructure teams to improve network boundaries, workload isolation, and access controls. Identity and access. Improve how people, services, and workloads authenticate and obtain access to infrastructure. Reduce unnecessary privileges, strengthen secrets management, and develop practical approaches to short-lived credentials and privileged access. Cloud and compute security. description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

GitLab’s Forward Deployed Engineering team is a field-situated product engineering function focused on strategic customer outcomes, artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, and direct contributions to GitLab’s product. This isn't a traditional field engineering, solutions architecture, or professional services role. As a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer, you'll work closely with customers while maintaining the technical standards and contribution discipline of a Staff-level product engineer.

You'll work where strategic customer urgency, complex technical ambiguity, and GitLab product execution intersect. You'll partner directly with strategic customers and teams across Product, Engineering, Support, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Solutions Architecture (SA), Customer Success Architecture (CSA), Customer Success Management (CSM), and Professional Services. You'll diagnose and resolve high-impact adoption blockers, contribute production-quality fixes and features, and turn what you learn into repeatable patterns for GitLab and its customers.

Why this role exists

Strategic customers sometimes encounter challenges that are too broad, deep, urgent, or cross-functional for any single team to own from start to finish. These challenges may involve product gaps, performance degradation, scale bottlenecks, AI governance, adoption blockers, architectural constraints, Git usage patterns, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) complexity, application programming interface (API) automation, security requirements, or operational instability.

Forward Deployed Engineering provides technical stewardship in these moments. The team doesn't simply observe, report, or escalate. You'll engage directly, diagnose the underlying technical problem, collaborate with the right teams, contribute code or technical solutions where appropriate, and transition the outcome into normal ownership once the customer is stable and the learning can be reused.

What you’ll do

Product contribution

  • Contribute production-quality code to GitLab’s product and adjacent systems.
  • Develop bug fixes, features, integrations, tooling, and performance improvements when strategic customer outcomes require direct engineering work.
  • Work within GitLab’s product and engineering processes, including issue discovery, merge request creation, testing, review, documentation, and maintainability.
  • Partner with Product and Engineering so customer-driven solutions support long-term product direction rather than becoming one-off customizations.
  • Turn blockers discovered in the field into durable product improvements, reference architectures, documentation, and repeatable implementation patterns.

Strategic technical stewardship

  • Engage with strategically important customers when adoption, retention, executive confidence, or public trust is materially at risk.
  • Diagnose complex problems across GitLab product behavior, customer architecture, Git internals, CI/CD workflows, API usage, observability, infrastructure, networking, and cloud environments.
  • Coordinate across Product, Engineering, SRE, Support, SA, CSA, CSM, Professional Services, and customer technical teams to drive resolution from discovery through handoff.
  • Provide recommendations grounded in data, traces, and systems analysis to improve GitLab usage, workflows, automation, and architecture.
  • Create durable outcomes without establishing permanent dependency on Forward Deployed Engineering.

AI adoption and agentic software development lifecycle

  • Drive governed, measurable, and production-oriented adoption of GitLab Duo Agent Platform with strategic customers.
  • Identify and resolve AI adoption blockers involving governance, usage controls, auditability, security, compliance, operating models, workflow design, and integrations.
  • Develop customer-safe adoption patterns for the agentic software development lifecycle (SDLC), AI-assisted development, intent-based review, AI governance, and human-in-the-loop software delivery.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Field, and Customer Success teams to turn AI adoption learning into reusable guidance and product improvements.

Thought leadership

  • Create technical narratives grounded in customer experience and product reality that can help shape the industry’s approach.
  • Contribute to Well-Architected Frameworks, whitepapers, webinars, reference architectures, technical strategy memos, and adoption frameworks.
  • Guide ideas through discovery, formulation, validation, amplification, and adoption across GitLab.
  • Partner with SA, CSA, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Product Marketing Management, CSM, Support, and executive stakeholders to make technical thought leadership a shared company capability.

What you’ll bring

  • Staff-level experience building, operating, or improving complex production software systems.
  • Experience contributing to large, mature product codebases with high standards for testing, maintainability, performance, and security.
  • Strong Ruby on Rails or Go experience and the ability to contribute directly to GitLab’s product and adjacent systems.
  • Experience with AI-assisted software development, agentic workflows, AI governance, model evaluation, context management, prompt and workflow design, or AI adoption in enterprise environments.
  • Experience diagnosing complex system behavior across application code, data stores, infrastructure, observability, networking, APIs, and customer usage patterns.
  • Deep knowledge of modern DevSecOps workflows, including Git, merge requests, CI/CD, security controls, compliance needs, and enterprise software delivery.
  • Experience working with strategic customers or senior technical stakeholders in ambiguous, high-impact situations.
  • The ability to coordinate across product, engineering, field, and customer teams without formal authority.
  • Strong written communication and sound judgment, including the ability to create technical narratives and distinguish reusable product work from customer-specific customization.

Strongly preferred qualifications

  • Direct experience with GitLab as a platform, including GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, or GitLab Self-Managed.
  • Production experience with Ruby on Rails, Go, PostgreSQL, Redis, Sidekiq, Vue, TypeScript, Kubernetes, Docker, Linux, or observability tools.
  • Deep familiarity with Git internals, repository performance, large-scale Git usage patterns, or GitLab Runner behavior.
  • Experience creating technical thought-leadership materials, such as whitepapers, technical talks, architecture frameworks, requests for comments, public technical writing, or internal strategy documents.
  • A background in performance engineering, site reliability engineering, platform engineering, infrastructure engineering, or distributed systems.
  • Experience working in open source or highly asynchronous engineering environments.

Technologies and domains

Directly relevant technologies and domains include:

  • Ruby on Rails
  • Go
  • AI-assisted development and the agentic SDLC
  • PostgreSQL
  • Redis and Sidekiq
  • Git internals
  • GitLab CI/CD and Runner architecture
  • Kubernetes and containers
  • Terraform
  • Linux, networking, observability, and performance analysis
  • Vue and TypeScript
  • APIs and automation
  • DevSecOps governance, security, and compliance

What this role is not

This role isn't:

  • A generic field engineering role.
  • A proof-of-concept factory.
  • A replacement for Solutions Architecture, Customer Success Architecture, Customer Success Management, Professional Services, Support, SRE, Product, or Engineering.
  • A customer-specific customization function.
  • Unbilled Professional Services.
  • A requirements-gathering role that only escalates to Product.
  • An AI evangelism role disconnected from product execution.

Success measures

Success in this role may include:

  • Stabilizing strategic customer adoption or retention risks.
  • Fixing product bugs or contributing features.
  • Removing AI adoption blockers for strategic accounts.
  • Creating reusable implementation patterns and transitioning them to long-term owners.
  • Producing or enabling Well-Architected Frameworks, whitepapers, webinars, or technical narratives.
  • Resolving cross-functional customer challenges without creating permanent dependency on Forward Deployed Engineering.
  • Equipping Product, Engineering, Support, CSA, CSM, Professional Services, and SA teams with better guidance based on learning from the field.
  • Increasing adoption and effective use of GitLab capabilities, especially GitLab Duo and GitLab Duo Agent Platform, in targeted accounts.

About the team

The Forward Deployed Engineering team connects strategic customer needs with GitLab product execution. The team works directly with customers and across GitLab to resolve complex adoption challenges, contribute durable product improvements, and create reusable technical guidance. Its goal is to stabilize urgent situations, improve the product, and transition ongoing ownership to the appropriate team rather than create a permanent dependency.

Ideal candidate profile

You're a Staff-level product or platform engineer who can operate in the field without becoming field-only. You're comfortable reading traces, writing production code, debugging architecture, discussing AI governance, leading a customer technical session, opening a merge request, outlining a whitepaper, and coordinating across teams to achieve a strategic customer outcome.

You're not simply a strong communicator with technical awareness. You're a credible engineer with the judgment, presence, and narrative ability to turn customer reality into product contributions, adoption guidance, and company-level thought leadership.

We welcome candidates with different backgrounds and levels of experience. Many successful candidates don't meet every qualification. If you're excited about this role, we encourage you to apply and let our recruiting team assess your application.

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

  • Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being
  • Flexible Paid Time Off 
  • Team Member Resource Groups
  • Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Growth and Development Fund
  • Parental Leave 

Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.

Country Hiring Guidelines: GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.  

Privacy Policy: Please review our Recruitment Privacy Policy. Your privacy is important to us.

GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. GitLab’s policies and practices relating to recruitment, employment, career development and advancement, promotion, and retirement are based solely on merit, regardless of race, color, religion, ancestry, sex (including pregnancy, lactation, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression), national origin, age, citizenship, marital status, mental or physical disability, genetic information (including family medical history), discharge status from the military, protected veteran status (which includes disabled veterans, recently separated veterans, active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans, and Armed Forces service medal veterans), or any other basis protected by law. GitLab will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. See also GitLab’s EEO Policy and EEO is the Law. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know during the recruiting process.

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover. Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI. Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate. Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale. About the team Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, e-commerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people. About the role We’re looking for experienced applied scientists in two tracks: pre-training, and post-training and continual learning. Each scientist will own a focused research direction within a track. The areas below describe the team’s research agenda; we are looking for depth in one or more of them. The role involves designing experiments, writing the code to run them, analysing results and developing training methods that other teams can use. Scientists own the research questions, training objectives and evidence needed to decide whether a change works, and work with ML engineers to turn successful experiments into reliable training runs. We are a team of around 30 engineers with a flat structure, working directly with portfolio companies to define problems, evaluate models and bring successful work into production. In the first three months, the expectation is to establish strong baselines in a chosen research area, develop and evaluate an improvement, and work with the relevant teams to test it in a downstream application. Track 1: Pre-training This track focuses on continued pre-training of open-weight models on commerce data, including how we represent that data, allocate training compute and transfer capabilities to smaller models. Research areas include: Studying scaling behaviour, data mixtures and compute allocation to decide what goes into the next training run. Developing mid-training methods, including data refinement, annealing schedules, context extension and alignment between text and semantic IDs for users, items and merchants. Designing training sequences from user histories, merchant catalogues and market data, and studying how representations transfer across companies, languages and commerce categories. Building synthetic data pipelines and measuring their contribution through controlled comparisons with real data. Distilling the base model into smaller models, including through on-policy distillation, and measuring the trade-offs between quality, inference cost and latency. Developing evaluations that help select pre-training runs and predict downstream performance, including checks for temporal leakage, generalisation to new users and items, and retention of existing capabilities. Tabular foundation models are a possible specialisation: pre-training and in-context learning on structured commerce data, using synthetic and real tables and comparing results with established tabular methods. Relevant experience includes continued pre-training or mid-training, data mixture research, scaling laws, tokenisation, entity representations, distillation, or tabular foundation models such as TabPFN and TabICL. Track 2: Post-training and continual learning This track focuses on adapting LCM to commerce tasks and learning from interactions after deployment. The goal is to turn signals from a continuous stream of billions of user sessions across the portfolio into regular updates to model weights, while retaining the capabilities the model has already learned. Research areas include: Developing post-training methods using supervised fine-tuning, preference optimisation such as DPO, and reinforcement learning with verifiable or learned rewards, including GRPO and PPO. Learning from session histories, searches, clicks, purchases, repeat orders and operator feedback. This includes data selection, credit assignment and reward design that account for exposure bias, delayed outcomes and the difference between observed engagement and incremental business value. Studying how to combine new interactions with historical data, how frequently to update models, when an update is ready for deployment, and how to preserve performance as user behaviour and catalogues change. Building RL environments with simulated users, catalogues and multi-step commerce tasks, including inspecting trajectories, validating rewards and testing whether improvements in simulation transfer to real interactions. Developing reward models and LLM-based graders, calibrating them against expert judgments and observed outcomes, and testing for reward hacking, sycophancy and excessive concentration on popular items. Training decision models for rankings, offers and promotions using contextual bandits or offline RL, with off-policy evaluation to estimate value and uncertainty, identify gaps in the available evidence and inform controlled online experiments. Developing automated experiments that propose and test changes to training methods, prompts, tools or agent control flow, evaluated on held-out tasks and regression tests before acceptance. Relevant experience includes language-model post-training, reinforcement learning, reward modelling, agent training environments, continual learning, or offline RL and bandits applied to real decisions. The training experience required will depend on the research direction. Responsibilities across both tracks Define success with portfolio teams and evaluate models against strong baselines, including existing production systems, accounting for inference cost, latency and the business outcome the model is meant to improve. Design reproducible experiments with appropriate ablations, uncertainty estimates and failure analysis, using future-period and held-out evaluations, and test whether offline improvements hold online. Work with data and engineering teams on provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy-aware handling of customer histories. Publish research and contribute models, benchmarks, environments and training methods to open source where the work and data can be shared. Mentor colleagues, review experiment designs and communicate findings clearly enough to support training and deployment decisions. Minimum qualifications A PhD or equivalent industry research experience in machine learning, computer science, statistics or a related field. At least five years of research or applied science experience in machine learning, including doctoral research, with hands-on experience designing and running model-training experiments. For Track 1, this should include pre-training or mid-training of language models. For Track 2, it should include language-model post-training, or reinforcement learning and decision-model training relevant to the specialisation. description: Looking for a new adventure? You’ve come to the right place. We're an Amsterdam-based team of 100 (and counting) with 25+ nationalities amongst us! A varied bunch of “Citizens of The World” with a wide range of skills and hundreds of thousands of kilometers under our travel belts. And we have something important in common (other than our very well-worn passports): We want to change the way people travel. And that's exactly what we're doing, with the travel app to plan, track, and relive trips in a smart and beautiful way. Polarsteps has over 23 million users already, but, for us, this is just the beginning. We have big plans for the future, and so we need even more talented and enthusiastic people to help us on our journey. Want to know more about us? Here you go. Your expedition at Polarsteps - Senior Data & Analytics Engineer Over the past 10+ years, Polarsteps has grown massively through word-of-mouth, thanks to our product and tech department building a top-quality user experience for all our travelers. As our first Senior Data & Analytics Engineer, you'll own the foundation that every data-driven decision at Polarsteps is built on. Product & growth teams run experiments and analyse the data every week, leadership need clear reports for investors, and all of that depends on data that is reliable, modelled and compliant. You'll set the direction for our data platform, bring structure to data governance, and own the data infra that helps our product managers, marketers and data scientists do their job even better. You'll work closely with the Head of Engineering on infrastructure and architecture, and with the Head of Growth and product teams on what the business needs from data. With 20M+ users and ratings of 4.8 and 4.7 on the app stores and features in multiple Google and Apple showcases, we've got an impressive past. But we're even more excited for the future, and you'll play a crucial role in building the data foundation that gets Polarsteps to 100M+ travelers around the globe. Your itinerary What your journey at Polarsteps will look like day-to-day. Own the data platform roadmap: set the strategy for our data infrastructure and warehouse, make the build-vs-buy and tooling calls, and oversee execution together with DevOps. Design, build and maintain scalable ingestion pipelines for both internal (product events, back-end data) and external sources (ad platforms, attribution, app store data). Build and maintain a clean, documented modeling layer (e.g. dbt) that serves as the single source of truth for analysts, data scientists and self-serving PMs. Lead data governance: define and enforce event naming and tracking standards, a schema change process, documentation, and dashboard ownership. Embed privacy in the data stack: make sure personal data is categorized, minimized and pseudonymized before it reaches downstream and third-party tools, in close collaboration with Legal Own the health of the stack: monitoring, alerting, data quality checks and cost management, so issues are caught before they reach stakeholders. Define who owns what across our data tooling (e.g. Mixpanel, our warehouse and BI layer), and help teams get the most out of self-serve analytics. Enable data enrichment to unlock deeper insights for Product and Growth. Explore how we can safely use LLMs (such as Claude) on top of our data for analysis and reporting. Act as the go-to data partner for Product, Engineering and Growth, and help grow the data function as Polarsteps scales. The equipment in your backpack What we're hoping you'll bring with you. ✅ 5+ years of experience in data engineering, analytics engineering or a hybrid data role, ideally in a B2C product or mobile app company. ✅ Strong SQL and Python, and hands-on experience modeling large event datasets in a modern warehouse (e.g. ClickHouse, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift). ✅ Experience with dbt and an orchestration tool such as Airflow or Dagster. ✅ Proven track record of bringing structure to data governance: tracking plans, event ownership, documentation and data quality. ✅ Experience with product analytics tools (e.g. Mixpanel, Amplitude) and BI tools (e.g. Metabase, Looker). ✅ Comfortable owning infrastructure decisions: cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure), infrastructure-as-code (e.g. Terraform), CI/CD for data. ✅ A pragmatic, ownership-driven mindset: you're happy to set the strategy and get your hands dirty, and you enjoy the hygiene work others tend to avoid. ✅ Excellent communication skills: you can explain trade-offs to engineers and to non-technical stakeholders alike. Bonus points if you have: ✨ Experience with mobile attribution or marketing data (e.g. AppsFlyer, SKAdNetwork, ad platform APIs). ✨ Experience with reverse ETL or CDPs (e.g. RudderStack, Twilio Segment). ✨ Experience with experimentation data and A/B testing infrastructure. ✨ Knowledge of GDPR and handling personal data responsibly in an analytics stack. 1st class Polarsteps extras Some cool things to make the journey extra sweet. A yearly free flight or train ride to a random location! Give our Teleporter a spin here. A shiny MacBook to work your magic on. Hybrid working, our way. Work from home and the office, we ask everyone to be in the office 2 days a week. It’s how we stay flexible, focused, and meaningfully connected in person. An extensive home office set-up, everything from noise-canceling headphones to a standing desk. 30 days of vacation (for adventures or sitting on the couch, it's up to you). Two paid Culture Days for days that are important to you but not recognized by the official Dutch calendar. The option to switch up your zoom background by working from another country for up to 8 weeks a year. A personal development budget for that curious mind of yours! A pension plan to help you save for those around-the-world retirement trips. Delicious daily team lunches. Awesome monthly parties, as well as team trips away. A lively office in downtown Amsterdam, with travel costs reimbursed. Free Polarsteps Travel Books to contain all your far-flung adventures. At Polarsteps, we believe the best products are built by people as diverse as the travelers using our apps! That's why we specifically encourage people underrepresented in the tech industry to apply for a role with us. Because we believe that diversity, be it age, race, sexual orientation, physical ability, ethnicity, or gender identity, makes both the world and the workplace better. description: About Genesis We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco, London and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration and the pursuits they love for their own sake. We're building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model and we are starting to put it to work with real customers. The role General-purpose robots learn from real, dexterous human work, the kind of data that does not exist on the internet. We capture it with our own collection hardware: a person wears it, does the work, and the robot learns to do it too. You will be a senior member of the team scaling our data collection operation in Paris, working closely with our Paris research and engineering teams and with the operation in the Bay Area. You will help lead the day-to-day execution and quality bar on the Paris floor while remaining deeply hands-on with data collection, teleoperation, task setup, and real-robot testing. You will wear our gloves and cameras, teleoperate our hardware, and take ownership of complex collection requests from setup through execution and quality review. You will work shoulder to shoulder with our model engineering and research teams, turning their requests into physical demonstrations and feeding what you learn on the floor back to them. You will be expected to operate autonomously, help guide and train other operators and contribute to how the Paris operation evolves as the team grows. This is a hands-on leadership role. You will not just run existing tasks: you will help shape how they are executed, how quality is measured, and how other operators are trained to deliver consistently. What you will do Help lead the Paris data collection floor. Set the execution and quality bar for day-to-day collection work and help the team scale effectively. Own complex collection setups. Take a loosely defined request and turn it into a working, repeatable collection task, including the setup, fixtures, props, environment, and procedure, with minimal support from engineering. Create high-quality training data. Wear our gloves and cameras, teleoperate our hardware, and produce precise demonstrations that can be used to train our models. Own the full collection workflow. Go beyond collecting the data itself: review and quality-check your work, identify unusable episodes, support annotation, and help ensure that what reaches research is trainable data. Build repeatable tasks. Turn new collection requests into clear, repeatable processes that can be executed consistently by other operators. Partner with research and model engineering. Translate their requests into physical collection tasks, share observations from the floor, and iterate with them on setups and collection strategy. Improve the operation. Identify when a fixture, station layout, procedure, or collection method can be improved and proactively help implement those improvements. Write and improve the playbook. Own SOPs, quality checks, and training materials that allow the Paris operation to scale while maintaining a consistent quality bar. Guide other operators. Help onboard, train, and mentor operators and reinforce consistent execution across the team. Run real-robot testing. Partner with reliability and engineering teams to test robots on the floor, document what you observe, and help surface issues. Own quality. Review your own work and the team's, take direct feedback, and keep raising the bar. What we are looking for You have done precise, repetitive physical work to a high quality bar and can explain what made your work good and how you measured it. This could include data collection, teleoperation, motion capture, robotics lab work, assembly, fine craft, or another hands-on technical environment. Hands-on robot or glove-based data collection experience is a strong plus, but not a requirement. This kind of data collection is new, and we will teach you our specific tools and approach. You build, not just run. Give you a vague request and a scrappy setup, and you can turn it into a clean, repeatable task with the right fixtures, environment, process, and written procedure. You can operate autonomously. You are comfortable taking ownership of complex collection tasks with limited day-to-day support from engineering. You understand quality beyond collection. You can review your work, recognize when collected data is unusable or below the quality bar, and understand why. You are ready to lead. You have trained, mentored, or led others doing hands-on work and want to help establish the execution and quality standard for a growing team. You work well with research and engineering teams. You can translate their requests into physical collection tasks and turn what you observe during collection into useful feedback. You have exceptional attention to detail. You notice the moment something about the setup, hardware, environment, procedure, or collected data is off. You are technically handy. You are comfortable with Linux, some Python scripting to automate repetitive work, and hardware assembly and troubleshooting. You are comfortable in a fast-moving environment. Hardware, processes, and collection methods will evolve quickly, and you are comfortable adapting while helping improve how the team works. You communicate well in English. You will work daily with teams in Paris and the Bay Area across time zones. French is a plus. Bonus: reliability testing. You have partnered with a reliability or test team on real-robot testing. Working conditions and role constraints Work takes place in production environments and technical laboratories. Prolonged standing and repetitive hand and arm movements while wearing collection equipment, including gloves, head-mounted cameras, and headsets, for extended periods. Handling and lifting of loads, including props, fixtures, robot equipment, and station equipment, up to 23 kg for station setup and reconfiguration. Why this role Real ownership. You will have meaningful ownership over how the Paris data collection floor operates and help set the standard the team grows toward. Hands-on leadership. You will remain close to the work while helping guide other operators, improve execution, and raise the quality bar. Build, not just execute. You will take ambiguous collection needs and turn them into reliable, repeatable tasks that can scale across the team. A clear growth path. As the operation scales, this role can grow toward leading or supervising teams of operators or toward broader project and program management responsibilities. The front line of the mission. The data you create, review, and improve is what teaches our robots to work. Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

description: Who We Are You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today. We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover. Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI. Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate. Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale. About the team Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, ecommerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people. About the role We’re looking for a senior data engineer to build and operate LCM’s training-data platform, covering acquisition, processing, synthetic generation, quality evaluation and dataset versioning. Our core data includes events, sessions, orders, catalogues and feedback, supplemented by external sources and generated examples. In our flat team of around 30 engineers, you’ll work with scientists and ML engineers to turn these sources into reproducible datasets and measure how changes to the data affect model performance. You’ll also build tools and agents that automate preparation, task design and quality analysis. In the first three months, we expect you to take ownership of a part of the platform, such as a pipeline, the dataset versioning layer or the quality checks, deliver a reproducible dataset that a research project uses in a training run, and work with scientists to measure how your data changes affect model quality. What the role involves Build acquisition and processing pipelines for portfolio data and relevant public and licensed sources, including connectors and content extraction. Turn commerce records into ordered histories and link behaviour to outcomes without leaking future information. Develop the shared platform for inspecting sources, configuring processing and publishing training datasets. Operate distributed workflows, monitor reliability and cost, and implement access controls and retention requirements. Work with scientists, engineers and the relevant teams on data provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy-aware handling of customer histories. Implement dataset versioning and lineage across source snapshots, processing code and dataset configurations, so releases can be reproduced and traced to the training runs that used them. Build quality checks for completeness, freshness, duplication, extraction accuracy and coverage. Combine automated checks with sampled review to investigate problems that aggregate metrics can miss. Provide tools for source tagging, sampling and weighting, and maintain evaluation datasets with temporal splits and overlap checks. Work with scientists on controlled comparisons to establish whether data changes improve model quality. Build synthetic data pipelines supporting pre- and post-training, including instruction examples, preference data and agent trajectories. Implement generation, validation, scoring and filtering. Work with the research team to measure how the generated data affects model performance, and manage generation throughput and cost. Build agents that turn catalogue sources into training datasets: propose tasks based on available data and target model capabilities, configure processing and generation, curate outputs and investigate quality failures. Keep agent actions traceable and validate proposed changes before dataset release. Minimum qualifications At least five years of relevant data engineering experience, including ownership of substantial production pipelines. Strong Python and SQL, with experience writing tested, maintainable code. Hands-on experience with distributed processing using Spark, Ray, Beam or a comparable framework. Experience with cloud storage, workflow orchestration and operating pipelines through source changes, failures and backfills. Practical knowledge of data quality, versioning and lineage, and the ability to translate evolving research requirements into reliable implementations. Preferred qualifications Experience with LLM datasets, commerce data, content extraction, synthetic data generation or agents for data tasks. Experience with AWS, Databricks or EMR. Strong distributed-data engineering experience is welcome without prior experience on an LLM team. What we offer Ownership of the platform supplying LCM’s training and evaluation data, with direct collaboration with researchers and ML engineers. Access to proprietary commerce datasets, distributed processing infrastructure and models for generation and evaluation. Scope to make technical decisions and build reusable tools across portfolio companies. Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems. Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants. A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role. Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro. If you’ve built data systems at scale and want to help shape what a foundation model can do, we’d like to hear from you. Tell us about something you’ve built, the challenges involved and the difference it made. Why Prosus? At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next. Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth. Build with backing. Curious about our perks and benefits? Take a look at this page. Our Diversity & Inclusion Commitment We respect the dignity and human rights of individuals and communities wherever we operate in the world. Building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome and can thrive is critical for us. We provide access to education, which helps everyone understand the important role they play and the positive impact they can have. Want to know more about life at Prosus? Strong project and stakeholder management across Product, Engineering, Marketing and Partnerships in a fast-moving, sometimes ambiguous environment. Passion for AI and the open-source ecosystem, with the curiosity to stay current as the field moves. Nice to have Fluency in French; other languages are a plus for regional programs. Hands-on experience building with LLMs (Python or TypeScript), or a public portfolio of projects on GitHub or Hugging Face. An existing network of developer creators, open-source maintainers or community leaders in the AI space. Experience with community platforms and tooling such as Discord bots, Discourse, Common Room, Orbit-style analytics or a CRM. description:
About us

GoCardless, a Mollie company, is a global leader in bank payments. Over 100,000 businesses, from start-ups to household names, use GoCardless to collect, manage and send bank payments through Direct Debit, real-time payments and open banking. With US$130bn+ processed annually across 30+ countries, we handle recurring and one-off payments without the chasing, stress, or expensive fees. Our end-to-end payment platform also features AI-powered solutions to improve payment success and reduce fraud, alongside connections to over 350 platforms businesses use everyday.

We are headquartered in the UK, with teams and operations spanning North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.  For more information, please visit www.gocardless.com and follow us on LinkedIn ----- is the leading payments and financial services partner for business, rooted in Europe, with global reach.

Platform Engineering at GoCardless

The Platform Engineering team is a unified, globally distributed team, currently located in London, Riga and Lisbon. We work with all other engineering teams to empower them to build, release, run and scale their products, with a strong focus on both strategic project delivery and operational excellence.

Our work is a balance of:

  • Project delivery: building new platform components, from initial design to deployment.
  • Operational support: keeping our systems healthy and stable through on-call rotations and incident management.
  • Business as usual: continuous maintenance, improvements, and support for audits and compliance.

The role

We’re looking for a Senior SRE with deep PostgreSQL expertise to own the reliability, performance and scalability of our database estate. Our databases sit at the heart of a payments platform, so slowdowns and outages directly affect our customers.

You’ll work across our self-managed Stolon clusters and our GCP Cloud SQL fleet. Joining Mollie gives us the opportunity to consolidate, modularise and rethink how we run production databases, and you’ll help us do that while keeping everything reliable.

What excites you  

  • Run our database fleet reliably. Keep our production databases healthy and stable through significant change, including moves between platforms.
  • Own performance and capacity. Right-size instances, tune connection limits and pooling (PgBouncer), memory and autovacuum settings, and fix slow queries, N+1s and unused indexes before customers feel them.
  • Own upgrades and change. Lead major-version database upgrades end to end with minimal downtime, and own safe schema migrations, data migrations and backfills.
  • Build in resilience. Reduce idle-in-transaction sessions, tighten statement timeouts, and design and test failover, replication and backup and recovery.
  • Make it observable. Build dashboards and alerts in Grafana, Prometheus and Datadog to track saturation, latency and connection health.
  • Partner with application teams. Help them use their databases well and improve their query patterns.
  • Respond and learn. Take part in on-call, mitigate live database incidents, and run root cause analyses to prevent repeats.

What excites us

Skills

  • Typically 5+ years of production experience running PostgreSQL, including high availability, replication, and backup and recovery
  • Deep knowledge of Postgres performance and tuning: internals (memory settings, autovacuum, locking) and connection pooling, including managing it in production and supporting it on call
  • Experience running production databases in the cloud, whether on managed services or self-managed on cloud infrastructure
  • Strong query analysis skills (EXPLAIN plans, indexing strategy)
  • Experience running major-version upgrades safely with minimal downtime
  • Experience managing infrastructure as code with Terraform or similar IaC tooling
  • Experience with monitoring and alerting (Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog or similar)
  • Experience writing code/working in software engineering teams
  • Experience with on-call and incident response
  • Ability to influence application teams

Nice to have

  • Experience with Stolon, or similar Postgres HA tooling
  • Experience with managed cloud Postgres (GCP CloudSQL, AWS RDS etc.)
  • Experience with Kubernetes, GKE and ArgoCD
  • Experience migrating databases between platforms
  • Experience with SLOs and error budgets
  • Experience in payments or financial services

Why it matters

We hope you’re enthusiastic about the infrastructure space and the impact your work can have on others. In this role:

  • You’ll work on a core system with direct, measurable impact on the reliability of the payments.
  • You’ll solve hard performance and reliability problems in systems that matter.
  • You’ll shape our database approach at a pivotal moment, as joining Mollie opens up choices about how we structure our estate.
  • You’ll have real influence on technical design and decisions, and the chance to raise the bar for those around you.
  • You’ll work closely with application teams and build easy-to-understand, maintainable tools and automation.

Tech stack and tools

  • PostgreSQL, Stolon, Cloud SQL, PgBouncer
  • Python, Ruby, Golang
  • Terraform, Atlantis
  • GCP
  • Kubernetes, GKE
  • GitHub, ArgoCD
  • Grafana, Prometheus, Datadog

We use a wide range of technologies and will never expect you to have experience with all of them.

Base salary range: £62,000 - £108,000

Base salary ranges are based on role, job level, location, and market data. Please note that whilst we strive to offer competitive compensation, our approach is to pay between the minimum and the mid-point of the pay range until performance can be assessed in role. Offers will take into account level of experience, interview assessment, budgets and parity between you and fellow employees at GoCardless doing similar work.

(some of) The good stuff

  • Wellbeing - stay healthy with dedicated support and medical cover
  • Lunch- based on the location, you either get a meal voucher or a paid lunch when working from the office
  • Work away scheme - gives you the option to work away from your country of residence for up to 20 working days in any 12-month period
  • Adaptive Working - allows you to work flexibly, around your lifestyle
  • Parental leave - to suit everyone embarking on life's great adventure
  • Learning Budget - lead your own development with an annual learning budget
  • Time off - generous holiday allowance + volunteer days for ERG events + one day off if you need to move house

Life at GoCardless  

We're an organisation defined by our values; We start with why before we begin any project, to ensure it’s aligned with our mission. We make it happen, working with urgency and taking personal accountability for getting things done. We act with integrity, always. We care deeply about what we do and we know it's essential that we be humble whilst we do it. Our Values form part of the GoCardless DNA, and are used to not only help us nurture and develop our culture, but to deliver impactful work that will help us to achieve our vision.

As of April 2025, we had 806 employees (GeeCees) globally, with 524 based in the UK, 163 based in Latvia and 119 across our other offices.

Sustainability

We’re committed to reducing our impact on the environment, leaving a more sustainable world for future generations. Check out our sustainability action plan here.

description:
RDQ427R369

At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business.

Our Developer Ecosystem organisation shapes how developers and the AI agents working for them build on the Databricks Data and AI Platform, from within the product to the tools they already use.

We are hiring an Engineering Manager to lead our declarative deployment framework, which turns data and AI projects into versioned, reviewable, repeatable software. It is one product with two entry points. Third-party developers use our open-source CLI from their IDEs, terminals, and CI/CD systems. First-party, they author, deploy and inspect the same projects inside the Databricks workspace. In both, AI agents increasingly do the work: coding agents drive the CLI, and our in-product AI assistant authors and deploys projects alongside the developer. Thousands of organisations run their CI/CD on it, and it is one of the fastest-growing parts of the platform.

The team owns the deployment engine and CLI, the in-workspace authoring and deployment experience, and the metadata service and deployment history that record every deployment. The hard problems are real infrastructure-as-code problems: reconciling declared and live state, making plans safe for humans and agents to approve, keeping visual authoring and code in sync, and shipping weekly releases that remain backwards-compatible for our largest customers.

The impact you will have:

  • Lead and grow the team: Manage a team of senior engineers across three closely connected areas (the deployment engine and open-source CLI, the in-workspace authoring and deployment experience, and deployment history and metadata), working with strong tech leads. Hire, coach and promote, and grow engineers into tech leads.
  • Make agentic development the default path: Shape how developers and AI agents author, validate and deploy projects, both inside the workspace and from the developer's own coding agent. Design the tools, skills and guardrails so agents get the same safety and auditability as humans.
  • Own the strategy and roadmap: Partner with Product and Design to set a multi-quarter roadmap for declarative deployment: agentic development, governed deployments and deployment history, enterprise CI/CD, and new resource coverage. Make the trade-offs explicit when the demand is larger than the team.
  • Raise the bar on execution and operational excellence: Run a predictable delivery process for a fast-moving, open-source product with frequent releases. Own reliability, on-call health, incident response and the quality bar for a tool customers depend on to ship to production.
  • Treat backward compatibility as a product feature: Lead engine and configuration migrations without forcing customers through a flag day, and communicate change clearly to customers, the community and field teams.
  • Lead across the platform: Drive alignment with the many platform teams whose resources and services the framework deploys, and with our sibling teams in Developer Ecosystem (SDKs, CLI, IaC provider, IDE). Make the whole toolchain feel like one product.

What we look for:

  • 5+ years managing software engineering teams, and 8+ years of software engineering experience overall.
  • A track record of building and shipping developer tools or platforms used by many external developers or internal teams, such as infrastructure-as-code, deployment or CI/CD systems, CLIs, SDKs, or internal developer platforms.
  • A deep understanding of declarative systems and deployment workflows: plan/apply, state management, drift and reconciliation, environment promotion, GitOps.
  • Enough technical depth to engage on architecture and trade-offs with senior and staff engineers, and to hold a high-quality bar for public, versioned interfaces.
  • Experience leading teams through ambiguity, with competing priorities from customers, partners and platform dependencies, and making clear calls.
  • Strong product sense and a customer-first mindset. You enjoy talking to developers, reading their issues, and turning feedback into roadmap.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including with executives, partner teams and an external developer community.

Stand-out experience:

  • Built or led teams on infrastructure-as-code or deployment platforms, e.g. Terraform, Pulumi, AWS CDK / CloudFormation, Kubernetes controllers, Argo CD / Flux / Helm, or Vercel / Netlify-style deploy platforms.
  • Managed an open-source developer tool with an active community and a frequent release cadence.
  • Shipped developer workflows for AI coding agents (CLI-first tooling, agent skills, MCP), or AI-assisted authoring.
  • Have managed managers or multiple teams (~15 to 20+ engineers), owned a multi-year platform strategy, and grown tech leads and managers.

Lead initiatives to improve data governance frameworks and ensure alignment with organizational goals. - Facilitate communication and coordination between cross-functional teams to promote data compliance and quality. - Mentor junior team members to support their professional growth and enhance team capabilities.
